raw_response:
Hmm, let me think about this year.

I've been doing this forty years, so I mostly know what to do. My boy works in the city now, so it's just me and the wife on the 15 mu. That's the main thing on my mind — we're not young anymore, and cotton especially is a lot of bending over, picking three or four times in the fall. I can't do as much cotton as I used to.

So here's how I split the land. I'll put 10 mu in wheat-maize like most folks around here — that's our food and our main income. The other 5 mu I keep in cotton. I used to do more cotton back when the kids were home to help pick, but 5 mu is about what me and the old lady can handle now. Cotton prices haven't been great but the subsidy helps, and I don't want to give it up entirely — it's what I know.

**Wheat first.** I plant early-to-mid October, after the maize comes off. Same as always. I use the regular wheat seed, not the expensive improved stuff — my cousin tried one of those new varieties two years back and it didn't do much better, so why pay more. Before planting I plow in about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's the 15-15-15 type, so maybe 7-8 kg of N in there, plus phosphorus. Then at returning green in spring, when the wheat starts growing again, I topdress urea, another 10 kg or so. If it's been dry I'll irrigate then too. I water the wheat maybe 3 times — once before winter if the ground is dry, once at returning green, once at heading. Well water costs money, the electricity adds up, so I don't water more than I need to. Should get around 400 kg per mu, that's what I usually get. Last year was 420, year before 390, about the same.

**Maize goes right after wheat harvest in June.** No time to plow properly — I just hire the fellow with the no-till planter, costs me maybe 30 yuan a mu, and he drills it right into the wheat stubble. Everyone does it this way now. I put compound fertilizer through the planter at sowing, then topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage, about 10-12 kg N total per mu for the season. Maize does pretty well here if we get the summer rains — sometimes I don't irrigate at all, sometimes once if July is dry. I aim for around 450 kg per mu. Less fertilizer than wheat because maize picks up nitrogen from the rain better, and I'm tight on cash after wheat.

**Cotton on the 5 mu.** Plant mid-to-late April. I buy the seed fresh each year, the Bt kind so I don't have to spray for bollworm as much. Plow the field before planting, put down compound fertilizer as base, about 25 kg per mu. Then topdress urea at flowering, another 10 kg. Cotton needs weeding — I do it by hand mostly, me and the wife, takes a lot of days. Spray for aphids and mites if I see them, and once for bollworm just in case. Water once or twice in the dry summer. Picking in September and October, three rounds, that's the hard part. Hope for 250 kg lint per mu, that's a decent year for me.

Total input cost... let me figure. Wheat-maize 10 mu, maybe 400 yuan a mu for inputs across both crops, that's 4000. Cotton 5 mu, more like 500 a mu because of seed and sprays, that's 2500. Call it 6500 total, roughly. I keep some cash aside for emergencies — the wife's medicine, or if the well pump breaks.
